Nina: Quick sync — Umbra wants a short perf validation to check our tail behavior for a multi-tenant prompt mix. Goal: sustain 120 qps steady with p50 < 70ms, p99 < 320ms; plus two 45s bursts to 900 qps within the test window. They also requested a short note on tokenization variance and how that affects cost. Can we run a hit-and-run tomorrow morning?

Sam: I can spin this up. Model: open-llama-7b-quant, typical prompt 200 tokens, gen 40 tokens. Important: Umbra emphasized they have variable prompt sizes (50-600 tokens) which will change effective tokens/sec. We'll run 3 profile runs: small, median, and large prompts.

Omar: Run plan:
- provision 4xA10G in us-east-1 and 2 loadgen m5.large each
- warm caches for 10m per profile
- steady 120 qps for 1h per profile
- inject two bursts: 900 qps for 45s at t+20m and t+40m
- log per-request tokens, latencies, and cost estimate per 1M tokens

PerfBot: scheduling jobs now. Use these simplified commands:
./harness --endpoint https://api.redwood.dev/v1/response --profile small.json --qps 120 --duration 60m
./harness --endpoint ... --qps 900 --duration 45s --concurrency 180

Sam: A few expected outcomes: small prompts (200 tokens total) will benefit most from batching -> better p50; large prompts will push memory and KV cache behavior and may reduce batching efficiency. We should produce a short table in the writeup: tokens/request | expected batching factor | estimated tokens/sec/GPU.

Nina: Also need a plain-English blurb for the security questionnaire: retention windows and whether request bodies are accessible to engineers. Keep it simple.

Omar: Security blurb: "By default, request bodies are redacted at the edge. Engineers only see anonymized traces and metrics. Full access to raw request bodies is gated by contractual agreements and logged in audit trails; Private deployments provide isolated logging and customer-owned KMS for encryption. Retention: metrics 30d, request traces 7d by default." 

Sam: I'll run a smoke at 03:00 UTC and then the full matrix starting 06:00 UTC tomorrow. Nina, can you confirm Umbra's timezone and the window? 

Nina: Confirmed. Thanks. Please post the perf dashboard + 1-page summary here.
